A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NovelQA and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. The shared dataset, evaluation procedures, and results can be matched reliably across the reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations, human performance and annotation agreement, evidence-recall experiments, and closed-book and positional analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds model evaluations, evaluator and distractor comparisons, evidence distributions, and evidence-distance correlations.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction pipeline, template-based and free-form annotation, GPT-4 distractor generation, and QA and evidence-recall procedures remain unchanged. Additional annotation explanations and diagnostic experiments do not establish a revision to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions use 2,305 questions from the same 89 English novels: 65 public-domain and 24 copyrighted books. Generative, multichoice, evidence-recall, and closed-book tasks already appear in v2. Moving closed-book evaluation from Appendix E.5 to Section 4.6 does not add task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 retains the five models in v2 Table 1 and adds GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Llama-3.1-8B, and Llama-3.1-70B. This substantially broadens the evaluated model comparison. The human baseline newly displayed in that table was already reported in v2.

E3.justification: New protocols compare GPT-4 versus Claude-2.1 distractors and cross-evaluate GPT-4o-mini and Claude-3.5 answers using both evaluators. Appendix C.4.5 also introduces a maximum-evidence-distance analysis. The existing end truncation, book-level question batching, zero temperature, prompts, and human evaluation design are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantive checks of distractor-generation bias, evaluator preference, evidence-position coverage, and the relationship between multi-hop accuracy and evidence separation (Appendices C.2.4, C.3, C.4.2, and C.4.5). These extend benchmark validation beyond the retained question-type, positional, closed-book, and error analyses. The detailed account of failed deployments and recovery with shorter inputs is removed.

E5.justification: Table 16 introduces Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall correlation estimation, with parenthesized statistical quantities that are not explained clearly. Existing Cohen's kappa reporting is retained. Neither additional repeated runs nor new seed or confidence-interval reporting is established.

E6.justification: v3 Table 2 adds multichoice/generative scores of 71.85/53.32 for GPT-4o-mini, 77.92/62.30 for Claude-3.5-Sonnet, 62.31/42.65 for Llama-3.1-8B, and 69.39/51.50 for Llama-3.1-70B; all five original model rows retain their values. New results also quantify evidence distributions, evaluator differences, distractor effects, and negative evidence-distance correlations. These are additional findings, not same-model performance improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4.5 newly defines a question's evidence distance as the maximum distance between its supporting evidence pieces. This is a limited mathematical definition supporting the new analysis; the existing dataset formulation remains unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions present the same manually annotated, exceptionally long English-novel QA benchmark and emphasize persistent weaknesses in detailed understanding, multi-hop reasoning, and evidence use beyond 100K tokens. Updated model names and performance examples support these retained claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix A shifts from API-access and deployment restrictions toward genre and contamination concerns and explicitly acknowledges evidence loss through truncation. New interpretations attribute early evidence concentration to narrative introductions, associate wider evidence separation with harder questions, and argue that objective questions limit evaluator bias. The principal positional and error interpretations remain intact.

D1.justification: v3 adds annotation instructions and consent details, documents vLLM alongside LMDeploy, and provides explicit Hugging Face dataset and Codabench evaluation access information. Existing prompts, hardware, batching, and temperature details remain available despite relocation. The explicit 100-case annotation-agreement sample size stated in v2 is omitted.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds explicit discussion and citations for NarrativeQA and NarrativeXL, contrasting their summary-based or automated question construction with NovelQA's expert annotation. v3 also adds the PagedAttention/vLLM citation and removes the YaRN and GLM-130B references associated with deleted deployment discussion. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The document undergoes substantial editorial reorganization: the abstract is rewritten, Advantages moves into the dataset overview, agreement details move into the main text, closed-book evaluation becomes Section 4.6, implementation settings move to the appendix, and the former separate supplementary sections are consolidated under Appendix C. Author information and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: v3 adds four analytical tables, expands the main model table, and moves the token-distribution figure, question-distribution table, pre/post-100K table, and closed-book table into the main text. Figure 7 is redrawn with paired length conditions and distinct colors. These changes substantially reorganize the visual presentation alongside the switch to the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, v3 provides broader model comparisons, useful benchmark-validity checks, clearer evidence-coverage limitations, and more actionable access information. These yield a modest net improvement. The gains are limited by unresolved reporting problems: Section 4.2 still calls GPT-4 the highest scorer despite Table 2, the new evaluator comparison excludes the stated GPT-4 judge, and Table 16 leaves its parenthesized statistics unexplained.
